questions.stem: What is the condition for a pair of linear equations in two variables to have infinitely many solutions?
choices: When the lines intersect at a single point
When the lines have different slopes
questions.solution: The correct condition is when the lines are coincident, meaning they overlap completely. If the lines are parallel, there are no solutions. If they intersect at a single point, there is a unique solution. If the lines have different slopes, they will intersect at one point, not be coincident.

questions.stem: Which of the following points lies on the graph of the equation 2x + y = 7?
questions.solution: Substituting x = 0 into 2x + y = 7 gives y = 7, so (0, 7) is a solution. Substituting x = 1 gives y = 5, not 6. Substituting x = 2 gives y = 3, not 4. Substituting x = 3 gives y = 1, not 2.

hi.solution: x = 0 के मान को 2x + y = 7 में प्रतिस्थापित करने पर y = 7 प्राप्त होता है, अतः (0, 7) एक हल है। x = 1 के मान को प्रतिस्थापित करने पर y = 5 प्राप्त होता है, जो 6 नहीं है। x = 2 के मान को प्रतिस्थापित करने पर y = 3 प्राप्त होता है, जो 4 नहीं है। x = 3 के मान को प्रतिस्थापित करने पर y = 1 प्राप्त होता है, जो 2 नहीं है।

questions.stem: What is the slope of a line that goes upward from left to right?
questions.solution: A positive slope indicates that as we move from left to right on a line, the line rises or goes upward. A negative slope would mean the line goes downward, a zero slope means the line is flat and horizontal, and an undefined slope means the line is vertical. Therefore, the correct answer is positive slope.

questions.stem: If a linear equation in two variables has a solution (–3, 4), what must be true about the equation?
choices: The equation must be of the form ax + by = 0
The equation must pass through the origin
The equation must have only one solution
The equation must satisfy the condition 3a + 4b = –2
questions.solution: The equation must satisfy 3a + 4b = –2 because substituting x = –3 and y = 4 into the equation ax + by = c results in –3a + 4b = c, which rearranges to 3a + 4b = –c. The other options are incorrect: the equation does not have to be of the form ax + by = 0, it does not necessarily pass through the origin, and a linear equation in two variables has infinitely many solutions, not just one.

choices: समीकरण के रूप ax + by = 0 होना आवश्यक है

समीकरण के लिए 3a + 4b = –2 की स्थिति पूरी होनी आवश्यक है
hi.solution: समीकरण के लिए 3a + 4b = –2 की स्थिति पूरी होनी आवश्यक है क्योंकि x = –3 और y = 4 को समीकरण ax + by = c में प्रतिस्थापित करने पर –3a + 4b = c प्राप्त होता है, जो 3a + 4b = –c में पुनर्व्यवस्थित किया जा सकता है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं: समीकरण के रूप ax + by = 0 होना आवश्यक नहीं है, यह आवश्यक नहीं है कि मूल बिंदु से गुजरे, और दो चरों में एक रैखिक समीकरण के अनंत हल होते हैं, केवल एक नहीं।

questions.stem: If the equation 3x + 2y = 12 is equivalent to y = –x + 6, which of the following must be true about their graphs?
questions.solution: The equation 3x + 2y = 12 can be rearranged to y = –x + 6, showing they represent the same relationship between x and y. This means their graphs are identical, so they are the same line. Parallel lines have different slopes, perpendicular lines have slopes that multiply to –1, and intersecting lines meet at one point, none of which apply here.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a solution to a pair of linear equations in two variables?
choices: A line that represents all possible solutions
An ordered pair that satisfies both equations
A single value that satisfies one equation
A graph that intersects at two points
questions.solution: The correct answer is an ordered pair that satisfies both equations, as this represents the point where the two lines intersect, fulfilling both equations simultaneously. A line that represents all possible solutions would describe a single equation, not a system. A single value that satisfies one equation does not account for both equations. A graph that intersects at two points would imply two separate solutions, which is not possible for a consistent linear system.

questions.stem: The point (2, 3) is the solution to a pair of linear equations. One of the equations is x + y = 5. Which of the following could be the other equation?
questions.solution: The point (2, 3) satisfies the equation x + y = 5. To find the other equation, we test the options: x + 2y = 8 gives 2 + 2×3 = 8, which is true. questions.stem: If the equations 10x – 5y = 20 and 4x – 2y = 8 are solved, how many solutions do they have?
questions.solution: The equations 10x – 5y = 20 and 4x – 2y = 8 are multiples of each other, meaning they represent the same line and thus have infinitely many solutions. If one equation can be obtained by multiplying the other by a constant, they are not independent and share all points on the line. The other options are incorrect because the equations are not parallel (which would mean no solution) or inconsistent (which would also mean no solution).
